message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of move‑in condition (photos, inventory list).
• Request written itemized statement if deposit is withheld. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep premises in good repair and free of health hazards. | • Document problems with photos and written notices.
• If landlord fails to fix, you may withhold rent or repair & deduct. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are limited to 10% of the monthly rent. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for residential leases >1 year.
• Lease must include: name of parties, address, rent amount, security deposit, lease term, pet policy, etc. | • Review lease carefully before signing; ask for clarification on ambiguous clauses. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month tenancy.
• For eviction: 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease violation, 60‑day notice for lease termination. | • Keep copies of all notices sent/received. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) except emergencies. | • If landlord enters without notice, you may file a complaint or seek damages. | | **Anti‑Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if discrimination occurs. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair after notice, tenant may repair and deduct cost from rent, or withhold rent. | • Keep receipts and document repairs. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow court procedure: serve proper notice, file unlawful detainer action, obtain judgment, and obtain sheriff’s writ. | • Tenants can contest eviction in court; they may also negotiate a settlement. | | **Pet Policy** | • Landlord may require a pet deposit or fee; cannot refuse pets unless it violates a federal or state law. | • Provide proof of pet vaccination and behavior. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Lease may restrict subletting; if allowed, tenant must get landlord’s written consent. | • Subletting without consent can lead to lease termination. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, electricity, and gas. | • If utilities fail, tenant may withhold rent or repair & deduct. | | **Fair Housing** | • Under the Fair Housing Act, landlords cannot impose different terms or conditions based on protected classes. | • Report violations to HUD or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written correspondence, and receipts are your best evidence. 2. **Know the Timeline** – Understand how many days’ notice are required for each situation. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send notices via certified mail or email with read receipt. 4. **Seek Legal Advice** – If disputes arise, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or local legal aid organization. 5. **File Complaints** – If you suspect discrimination or illegal eviction, file complaints with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). ### Resources - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – [https://www.tchra.texas.gov](https://www.tchra.texas.gov) - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Legal Aid of North Texas** – [https://legalaid.org](https://legalaid.org) - **Texas Property Code, Chapter 24** – Official text available at the Texas Legislature website. If you have a specific issue (e.g., landlord withholding deposit, dispute over repairs, or potential discrimination), let me know and I can give more tailored guidance or help draft a formal letter to your landlord.
